title: Reward, Wanting vs. Liking, & The Mesolimbic Dopamine Circuit
description: Explore motivation neurocircuitry: VTA-to-NAc dopamine, Berridge's wanting vs. liking, Schultz's reward prediction error, and addiction.

slides.title: The Mesolimbic Dopamine Pathway: The Engine of Desire 🎯
slides.content:
# The Brain's Incentive Highway

In 1954, James Olds and Peter Milner made a serendipitous discovery: rats would press a lever thousands of times an hour—ignoring food, water, and sleep until exhaustion—to receive electrical stimulation in the medial forebrain bundle. They had discovered the **brain's reward circuit**.

### The Mesolimbic Dopamine Pathway:
* **Origin**: Dopaminergic neurons in the midbrain **Ventral Tegmental Area (VTA)**.
* **Projection**: Axons project via the medial forebrain bundle to the **Nucleus Accumbens (NAc)** in the ventral striatum and the ventromedial prefrontal cortex.
* **Function**: Computes incentive salience, motivation, and reinforcement learning.

slides.title: Kent Berridge: Wanting vs. Liking 🍬
slides.content:
## Dissociating Desire from Pleasure

For decades, dopamine was popularly mislabeled as the 'pleasure molecule.' Neuroscientist **Kent Berridge** proved that motivation consists of two distinct neurobiological systems:

| Feature | 'Wanting' (Incentive Salience) | 'Liking' (Hedonic Impact) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Psychological State** | Craving, motivation, pursuit, cue reactivity | Consummatory pleasure, sensory delight, satisfaction |
| **Neural Substrate** | **Mesolimbic Dopamine** (VTA $\rightarrow$ Nucleus Accumbens) | **Endogenous Opioids & Cannabinoids** in discrete **'Hedonic Hotspots'** (NAc shell and ventral pallidum) |
| **Effect of Dopamine Depletion** | Animal will not work or walk to get food (zero wanting) | When sweet sugar is placed directly on tongue, animal still shows full hedonic facial licking (intact liking!) |
| **Relevance to Addiction** | Sensitized: Massive craving and pursuit | Diminished: Tolerance reduces actual pleasure |

quizData.question: What happens when dopamine in the nucleus accumbens of a laboratory animal is completely depleted?

options.text: The animal loses motivation to seek food ('wanting'), but still exhibits full hedonic pleasure ('liking') when sweet food is placed in its mouth
The animal violently rejects all sweet tastes with disgust faces
The animal permanently loses all hearing and vision
The animal enters an irreversible coma

quizData.explanation: Berridge proved that dopamine mediates incentive motivation ('wanting'), whereas hedonic pleasure ('liking') is mediated by opioid hotspots.

slides.title: Wolfram Schultz & Reward Prediction Error (RPE) 📊
slides.content:
## Dopamine is Not Reward: It is the Surprise of Reward!

Neurophysiologist **Wolfram Schultz** recorded from midbrain dopamine neurons during classical conditioning:

1. **Unpredicted Reward**: Dopamine neurons burst fire with intense excitement when an unexpected reward appears ($RPE > 0$).
2. **Learned Conditioned Stimulus (CS)**: After pairing with a light or tone, the dopamine burst **shifts backward in time** to the cue itself! When the predicted reward arrives, neurons fire at normal baseline ($RPE = 0$).
3. **Reward Omission**: If the cue appears but the promised reward is withheld, dopamine neurons **completely pause firing** below baseline at the exact moment the reward was expected ($RPE < 0$).

*Takeaway*: Dopamine encodes **Reward Prediction Error**—the mathematical difference between what happened and what was expected, driving reinforcement learning!

quizData.question: In Wolfram Schultz's electrophysiological experiments, what do midbrain dopamine neurons do when an expected reward is omitted?

options.text: They temporarily suppress and pause their firing below baseline at the expected delivery time
They fire twice as many action potentials as before
They instantly undergo apoptosis and die
They convert into GABAergic inhibitory neurons

quizData.explanation: When an expected reward is withheld, a negative prediction error occurs, causing a sharp dip/pause in dopaminergic firing below baseline.
